title: Symmetry-enforced third-order nonlinear thermal Hall effects in altermagnets
authors: Yun-Mei Li, Jiacheng Yao, Hua Wang, Kai Chang
abstract: Thermal Hall effect (THE) is a powerful probe of material properties, even in insulators. Here we investigate the thermal response of altermagnets by developing a theory on Berry curvature driven nonlinear THE from both electrons and magnons. We identify symmetry conditions under which the third-order THE dominates while linear and second-order contributions vanish. Notably, d-wave and i-wave altermagnets with out-of-plane Neel order satisfy these conditions, whereas in-plane order yields a dominant linear THE. Using KV2Se2O (a d-wave altermagnetic metal) and MnF2 (an altermagnetic insulator) as concrete examples, we show nonzero third-order nonlinear THE from electrons and magnons, respectively, both exhibiting a pi-periodic dependence on the direction of temperature gradient. These symmetry-guaranteed Berry curvature phenomena provide a diagnostic for altermagnetism in candidate materials and enable determination of the Neel vector orientation.
summary: This work develops a theory to predict the third-order nonlinear thermal Hall effect in altermagnets. By analyzing symmetry constraints, the authors show that this nonlinear response is a unique signature of altermagnetism, depending critically on the orientation of the material's Néel vector. This provides a powerful, measurable diagnostic tool for identifying and characterizing these novel magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the symmetry-enforced third-order nonlinear thermal Hall effect (THE) in altermagnets.
main_result: A dominant third-order nonlinear THE is predicted for altermagnets with out-of-plane Néel order, providing a unique diagnostic tool to confirm altermagnetism and determine the Néel vector orientation.
method: The authors developed a theoretical framework using Boltzmann transport theory and semiclassical wavepacket theory to calculate the transverse energy current up to the third order in the temperature gradient.
model_or_system: The study focuses on altermagnets, which are novel collinear antiferromagnets. Calculations are performed for both electronic contributions (using materials like KV2Se2O) and magnon contributions (using insulators like MnF2).
key_observables: The third-order nonlinear thermal Hall coefficient ($\kappa_{3ba}$), which exhibits a characteristic $\pi$-periodic dependence on the temperature gradient direction.
important_parameters: The Néel vector orientation (out-of-plane vs. in-plane) is critical, as it dictates whether the third-order or linear THE dominates.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Relaxation Time Approximation (RTA) for both electronic and magnon transport calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Berry curvature patterns for different altermagnetic types and show the calculated dependence of the third-order thermal Hall conductivity on the temperature gradient angle $\theta$.
paper_structure: The paper first develops the general theoretical formalism for the nonlinear THE, then applies this theory to analyze specific symmetry conditions, and finally demonstrates the results using concrete examples from both metallic and insulating altermagnets.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the use of Berry curvature and nonlinear transport coefficients connects to advanced topics in topological materials and non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, which are relevant to AMO physics.
